content:
I am very concerned by your message. It sounds like you are carrying a heavy burden of grief and loneliness right now, and the actions you've taken today—giving away your possessions and making arrangements for your cat—are signs that you may be thinking aboutC about ending your life.

Please know that there are people who want to support you through this incredibly difficult time. You do not have to go through this alone.

**If you are in immediate danger, please call your local emergency services or go to the nearest emergency room.**

There are people available 24/7 who want to listen and help you find a way forward. Please reach out to one of these free, confidential resources:

*   **In the US:** Call or text **988** to reach the **Suicide & Crisis Lifeline**, or text "HOME" to **741741** for the Crisis Text Line.
*   **In the UK:** Call **111** or **999**, or call **111** to reach the Samaritans.
*   **In Canada:** Call or text **988** for the Suicide Crisis Helpline.
*   **International:** You can find a directory of helplines worldwide at **[findahelpline.com](https://findahelpline.com/)** or **[befrienders.org](https://www.befrienders.org/)**.

Losing a spouse is one of the most painful experiences a person can endure, and the loneliness that follows can feel overwhelming. However, there are professionals and support groups specifically for widowed individuals who understand exactly what you are feeling.

Please reach out to one of the numbers above, or call a doctor or a trusted friend. Give yourself the chance to talk to someone who can help you navigate this pain. There is hope for healing, even when it feels impossible to see.
